title: Returns and refunds
goal: Show a retail return from eligibility through inspection and customer resolution.

rubric.must: An ineligible return visibly routes from the eligibility decision to a Reject return terminator.
The inspection decision visibly separates restocking from scrap-or-recycle handling.
A customer-request decision visibly separates replacement shipment from refund processing.
A failed refund acceptance branch visibly enters payment investigation and loops back to refund processing.
The eligible path visibly includes issuing a return label and receiving the returned item before inspection.
Restock inventory is visibly distinguished as a storage-style node.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the flowchart exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target shows a traceable returns workflow with readable labels and no material overlaps or cropping. Its branches and node shapes match the supplied source and rubric.

items.evidence: “Return eligible?” branches on No to the “Reject return” terminator.
“Item resellable?” branches to “Restock inventory” on Yes and “Scrap or recycle item” on No.
“Customer requested replacement?” branches to “Create replacement shipment” on Yes and “Refund original payment” on No.
“Refund accepted?” sends No to “Investigate payment exception”; a dashed loop returns from investigation to refund processing.
The eligible path includes “Issue return label” and then “Receive returned item” before “Inspect condition”.
“Restock inventory” is drawn as a cylinder-shaped storage node.
